title: Emergency fund
tags: emergency fund rainy day job loss liquid buffer
text: Keep 3 to 6 months of living costs (including EMIs) in a savings account, liquid fund or FD before you invest for growth. It stops one bad month from forcing you to borrow or sell investments at a loss.

title: Budgeting (50-30-20)
tags: budget budgeting spend expenses save saving salary plan 50 30 20
text: A simple starting split is 50% needs, 30% wants and 20% savings and investments. Automate the 20% on salary day so saving happens before spending.

title: Compounding and starting early
tags: compound compounding interest early start time grow delay
text: Returns earn their own returns, so time matters more than amount. Money invested in your twenties can end up several times larger than the same amount invested ten years later.

title: Inflation
tags: inflation prices rising real return purchasing power
text: Prices in India have historically risen around 5 to 6% a year, so money that earns less than that loses buying power. Compare every return after inflation and tax.

title: Fixed deposits (FD)
tags: fd fixed deposit bank term deposit safe interest
text: An FD pays a fixed rate for a fixed term. It is low risk and good for short-term goals and emergency money, but the interest is taxed at your slab rate and often only just beats inflation. Bank deposits are insured up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank.

title: Public Provident Fund (PPF)
tags: ppf public provident fund government 15 year tax free
text: PPF is a government-backed 15-year savings scheme. You can put in Rs 500 to Rs 1.5 lakh a year, the rate is set by the government every quarter, and the interest and maturity amount are tax free. Partial withdrawals are allowed after a few years.

title: Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)
tags: epf pf provident fund employer salary uan eps
text: Salaried employees put 12% of basic pay into EPF and the employer matches it (part goes to the pension scheme, EPS). The rate is declared each year. Check your UAN passbook to confirm your employer is actually depositing.

title: National Pension System (NPS)
tags: nps national pension system retirement pfrda tier annuity
text: NPS is a low-cost, market-linked retirement account regulated by PFRDA. You choose a mix of equity, corporate bonds and government bonds. At retirement part of the corpus is paid as a lump sum and the rest buys a pension (annuity).

title: Mutual funds and SIPs
tags: mutual fund mf sip systematic investment plan nav equity debt fund
text: A mutual fund pools money and invests it for you. A SIP invests a fixed amount every month, which averages your buying price and builds a habit. Equity funds suit goals five or more years away; returns are not guaranteed.

title: Index funds
tags: index fund nifty sensex passive etf low cost beginner
text: An index fund simply copies an index such as the Nifty 50. Costs are low and you get instant diversification, which makes it a sensible default for beginners.

title: Stocks
tags: stock stocks share shares equity market trading demat
text: A share is part-ownership of a company. Prices can swing sharply, so use only money you will not need for at least five years, spread it across companies and avoid tips and intraday bets.

title: Gold
tags: gold jewellery etf hedge
text: Gold tends to hold value when markets or the rupee fall. Many planners keep about 5 to 10% in gold, preferably through gold ETFs or gold funds, which avoid making charges and storage risk.

title: Property
tags: property real estate house flat home rent land
text: Property is a large, illiquid asset: slow to sell and costly to maintain. Do not count the home you live in as retirement money unless you plan to sell or downsize.

title: Term life insurance
tags: term insurance life cover dependents family protection premium
text: Term insurance is pure life cover and the cheapest way to protect dependents. A common rule is cover worth 10 to 15 times your annual income. Avoid mixing insurance with investment.

title: Health insurance
tags: health insurance medical mediclaim hospital cover family floater
text: One hospital stay can wipe out years of savings. Keep your own health policy in addition to any employer cover, because employer cover ends when the job does.

title: Loans, EMIs and credit cards
tags: loan loans emi debt credit card interest prepay borrow
text: Try to keep all EMIs together under about 40% of take-home pay. Pay off the highest-interest debt first; credit cards can charge 36% a year or more, so never pay only the minimum due.

title: Credit score
tags: credit score cibil report rating
text: Your credit score runs from 300 to 900 and a score above roughly 750 gets better loan rates. Pay every bill on time and use well under a third of your card limit.

title: Income tax: old versus new regime
tags: tax regime old new 80c 80d deduction slab save saving income
text: The new regime is the default: lower rates but few deductions. The old regime allows deductions such as 80C (up to Rs 1.5 lakh), 80D (health insurance) and 80CCD(1B) (Rs 50,000 for NPS). Employer NPS contributions under 80CCD(2) are deductible in both. Work out your tax both ways before choosing.

title: ELSS (tax-saving funds)
tags: elss tax saving mutual fund lock-in 80c
text: ELSS funds are equity mutual funds with a three-year lock-in that qualify for the 80C deduction under the old tax regime.

title: Asset allocation and diversification
tags: asset allocation diversify diversification risk rebalance mix portfolio where invest
text: Spread money across equity, debt and gold according to when you need it and how much swing you can stomach. Money needed within three years belongs in FDs or debt funds; long-term money can take more equity. Rebalance once a year.

title: ESOPs
tags: esop esops employee stock option rsu vesting
text: ESOPs give you the right to buy your employer's shares. They can be valuable but tie your wealth to the same company that pays your salary, and tax is due both when you exercise and when you sell.

title: How much you need to retire
tags: retire retirement corpus need enough how much 25x rule fire
text: A rough target is 25 to 30 times your yearly spending at retirement, adjusted for inflation. The earlier you start and the more you step up contributions each year, the smaller the monthly amount needed.

title: Scams and fraud
tags: scam fraud otp phishing kyc guaranteed returns ponzi fake
text: No bank or regulator will ask for your OTP, PIN or password. Guaranteed high returns are a red flag. Check that an adviser or platform is SEBI-registered, and report fraud at once on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
